title: How to Get Cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews
dek: How to get cited by AI answer engines like ChatGPT search, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews: open crawler access, answer-first pages and trust signals.
keywords: get cited by AI answer engines
how to get cited by ChatGPT
how to show up in AI answers small business
summary: To get cited by AI answer engines, let their search crawlers reach your site, put a plain answer at the top of each important page, and back it with a named author and current facts. Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT search and Perplexity all pick sources from pages they can crawl and trust. There is no form to submit.

takeaways: AI answer engines cite pages they can crawl, index and trust, and none of them offer a submission form.
Blocking OAI-SearchBot or PerplexityBot in robots.txt keeps your pages out of ChatGPT search answers and Perplexity results.
Google says a page needs to be indexed and eligible for a snippet to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, with no extra technical requirements.
The pages that get cited put a direct answer in the first two sentences and back it with specific, checkable facts.
Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools now both report on AI search visibility, so you can measure progress instead of guessing.

body.heading: What does it mean to get cited by an AI answer engine?
paragraphs: Getting cited means an AI tool reads your page, uses it to build an answer, and shows your business as a source with a link. It is the AI version of ranking on page one. The person asking may never click, but your name and your answer reach them together.

A citation is not an ad and it is not a directory listing. You cannot bid on it or buy it. The system picks sources the way a careful researcher would, by judging which pages answer the question clearly and which ones it can trust.

Citations also send a different kind of visitor. Someone who clicks through from an AI answer has usually read a summary already, so they arrive further along in their decision and with a narrower question.

It is also not a one time win. You can be cited for one question and skipped for the next, even from the same page. If you want the bigger picture first, start with [what answer engine optimization is](/daily/what-is-answer-engine-optimization).

body.heading: How do Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT search and Perplexity choose sources?
paragraphs: Each tool searches the web, picks a handful of pages that answer the question, and summarizes them with links. The details differ by tool, but all three depend on being able to reach and read your page first.

subsections.heading: Google AI Overviews and AI Mode
paragraphs: Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode pull from the same index as regular Google Search. [Google Search Central](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) says a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet, and that there are no additional technical requirements. Both features may run several related searches behind the scenes, which Google calls query fan-out, before writing a response.

subsections.heading: ChatGPT search
paragraphs: ChatGPT search uses a crawler called OAI-SearchBot. [OpenAI's crawler documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers. OpenAI recommends allowing it in robots.txt if you want to appear.

subsections.heading: Perplexity
paragraphs: Perplexity uses PerplexityBot to surface and link websites in its results. [Perplexity's crawler page](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/resources/perplexity-crawlers) recommends allowing it in robots.txt and says changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.

body.heading: What has to be true before any AI tool can cite you?
paragraphs: Your page has to be reachable, indexed and readable as text before content quality matters at all. Work through these in order, because each one can quietly block everything after it.

Step 1: Open your robots.txt file and confirm you are not blocking Googlebot, Bingbot, OAI-SearchBot or PerplexityBot. Check your hosting or security plugin too, since some block bots without telling you.
Step 2: Confirm your key pages are indexed using the URL Inspection tool in Google Search Console. A page Google has not indexed cannot appear in AI Overviews.
Step 3: Make sure no page you care about uses noindex or nosnippet by accident. Those controls also limit what Google can show in its AI features.
Step 4: Put the important answers in real text on the page. A price list trapped in an image or a PDF is much harder for any system to quote.

body.heading: What makes a page worth citing?
paragraphs: A page earns citations when it answers one question clearly and gives the system reasons to trust it. Four habits do most of the work.

subsections.heading: A direct answer up top
paragraphs: Put a two or three sentence answer right under the heading, before any backstory. A thorough page is fine as long as the short answer comes first. Our guide on [how to write pages answer engines quote](/daily/write-pages-answer-engines-quote) covers this in detail.

subsections.heading: Specific, checkable facts
paragraphs: Specific facts beat general claims. We serve the whole county tells a system very little, while a list of the towns you serve gives it something it can repeat with confidence.

subsections.heading: A named author and honest dates
paragraphs: A real person with a real title, plus a published and updated date, helps readers and machines judge whether to trust the page. Undated, unsigned pages compete at a disadvantage.

subsections.heading: The same business facts everywhere
paragraphs: Your name, address, phone number and hours should match across your site and your Google Business Profile. Google's own guidance tells site owners to keep Business Profile information up to date, and it matters even more for [local searches that trigger AI Overviews](/daily/local-seo-ai-overviews).

body.heading: Is chasing AI citations worth it for your business?
paragraphs: For most service businesses, yes, because the work that earns citations is the same work that improves regular search results. Whether it deserves time this month depends on where you are starting.

subsections.heading: It makes sense if
paragraphs: It makes sense if customers research before they call, if they ask the same questions over and over, or if competitors already show up when you test AI tools. It also makes sense if your site is already indexed and you just need clearer pages.

A business whose customers compare several options before choosing, such as a contractor, a clinic or a law office, usually gains the most, because those buyers ask long, specific questions that AI tools are built to answer.

subsections.heading: Skip it for now if
paragraphs: Skip it for now if your site is not indexed, loads slowly, or still has an outdated phone number on it. Fix those basics first, since no AI tool will cite a page it cannot reach or trust.
The same goes for a site that has no pages answering real customer questions yet. Build a few strong service pages first, then come back to citations once there is something worth citing.

subsections.heading: A worked example: a roofing company
paragraphs: Here is a worked example with simple numbers, not a statistic. Picture a roofing company that lists the 20 questions customers ask most before booking, then groups them onto 5 pages: repair, replacement, storm damage, insurance claims and service area.

Rewriting each page with an answer-first opening, question headings and a named author takes about 30 minutes, so 5 pages take about 2.5 hours. Each month, the owner asks 5 of those questions in Google AI Mode, ChatGPT search and Perplexity, which is 15 checks and about 20 minutes of work.

If the company is cited in 3 of 15 checks in month one and 6 of 15 in month three, citation rate moved from 20 percent to 40 percent. That simple tally tells the owner which pages are working and which need another pass.

body.heading: Which questions should you try to get cited for?
paragraphs: Aim for the questions customers ask right before they decide to buy, not broad topics where national publishers already dominate. A local electrician is unlikely to be cited for what is electricity, but has a real shot at how much does it cost to add an outlet in a finished basement.

subsections.heading: Questions from your own inbox
paragraphs: The best list comes from emails, call notes and chat logs. If three customers asked it this month, other people are asking an AI tool the same thing.

subsections.heading: Comparison and decision questions
paragraphs: Google says AI Mode is especially helpful for questions that need comparison and reasoning. Pages that compare options honestly, like repair versus replacement, fit that kind of question well.

subsections.heading: Local and specific questions
paragraphs: Questions that include a town, a product model or a specific situation have fewer strong answers competing for them. That gives a small business with real local knowledge a better chance of being the clearest source.

subsections.heading: Questions you can answer better than anyone
paragraphs: Look for topics where you have firsthand experience, such as what an inspection actually checks or how long a job really takes in your area. Specific experience is hard for a generic page to copy, and it gives an AI system a reason to choose you.

body.heading: What are the most common mistakes?
paragraphs: Most missed citations come from a handful of fixable errors, not from a lack of content.

subsections.heading: Blocking the search crawlers
paragraphs: Some sites block every AI bot to keep content out of model training, then wonder why they never appear in AI answers. OpenAI lists OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot as separate settings, so you can allow search while still opting out of training.

subsections.heading: Burying the answer
paragraphs: Three paragraphs of company history before the answer is the most common page problem we see. Move the answer up and keep the history below it.

subsections.heading: Chasing shortcuts
paragraphs: Google's guide to [optimizing for generative AI features](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) says Google Search ignores llms.txt files and that seeking inauthentic mentions is not as helpful as it seems. Time spent on tricks is time not spent on better pages.

subsections.heading: Fixing every page at once
paragraphs: A rushed pass across 60 pages teaches you less than getting 5 revenue pages exactly right. Start small, measure, then expand.

body.heading: How do you know if it is working?
paragraphs: You can now measure AI visibility with free first-party tools, plus a few simple manual checks. Use them together, since no single report covers every AI tool.

subsections.heading: Google Search Console
paragraphs: Google Search Console has a [generative AI performance report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139?hl=en) that shows impressions from AI Overviews and AI Mode. Google says it rolled out to all websites on August 31, 2026.

subsections.heading: Bing Webmaster Tools
paragraphs: Bing Webmaster Tools has an AI Performance report that shows how often Microsoft Copilot and Bing's AI answers cite your pages. It also lists grounding queries, the phrases the AI used to find your content.

subsections.heading: Analytics and spot checks
paragraphs: OpenAI says ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to referral links, so ChatGPT search visits can show up in Google Analytics. [Search Engine Land reported](https://searchengineland.com/chatgpt-appears-to-drop-utm-tracking-making-ai-referral-traffic-harder-to-measure-496552) in October 2026 that some ChatGPT links now arrive without that tag, so part of that traffic can show up as direct. Pair that with monthly spot checks in Perplexity and ChatGPT. Our guide to [measuring AI search visibility](/daily/measure-ai-search-visibility) walks through the full setup.

faq.question: Do I need to submit my website to ChatGPT or Perplexity?
faq.answer: No. Neither offers a submission form. They find pages through their own crawlers, OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot, so allowing those in robots.txt is what matters.

faq.question: Can I pay to be cited in AI answers?
faq.answer: No. Citations in AI Overviews, ChatGPT search and Perplexity cannot be bought. Ads, where they exist, are labeled separately from the cited sources.

faq.question: Do I need an llms.txt file to show up in Google AI Overviews?
faq.answer: No. Google says Google Search ignores llms.txt and that no special files or markup are needed for its AI features. It does not hurt to keep one for other tools.

faq.question: How long does it take to start getting cited?
faq.answer: It varies by page and question. Crawler changes in robots.txt can take about 24 hours to register with OpenAI and Perplexity, but earning citations depends on how well your page answers the question compared with others.

faq.question: Does schema markup make AI tools cite me?
faq.answer: Not on its own. Google says no special schema is required for AI Overviews or AI Mode, but accurate structured data helps systems read your page correctly. See our [schema markup guide](/daily/schema-markup-for-ai-answers).
